Template.title: Template
Template.description: Represents a user-defined document template, categorized by type (e.g., Quote, Invoice, Contract), used to generate dynamic documents.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Template entity.

name.description: The user-defined name for the template.

type.description: The type of the template, indicating its purpose (e.g., 'Quote', 'Invoice', 'Contract').

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the template was first created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the template was last updated.

createdByUserId.description: Reference to the unique identifier of the user who created this template. (Relationship: User 1:N Template)

DocumentTemplateContent.title: DocumentTemplateContent
DocumentTemplateContent.description: Stores the structured content and layout definition for a specific Template, enabling 'word document'-like functionality with dynamic data bindings.

id.description: Unique identifier for the DocumentTemplateContent entity.

templateId.description: Reference to the Template this content definition belongs to. (Relationship: Template 1:1 DocumentTemplateContent)

documentLayoutJson.description: A serialized JSON string representing the entire layout and content structure of the document template. This includes pages, sections, elements (text, images, tables), their styling, positions, and data binding specifications to external 'module' fields.

definition.description: Collection for storing user-specific document templates (Quote, Invoice, Contract types). Each document represents a template created by the user identified by '{userId}'. This collection enforces path-based ownership, with 'createdByUserId' matching the '{userId}' wildcard. Includes 'createdByUserId' for authorization.

A specific document representing a template owned by the user '{userId}'. Contains the template's name, type, and metadata. The 'createdByUserId' field in the document must match '{userId}' in the path. Includes 'createdByUserId' for authorization.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns this template.

params.name: templateId
params.description: The unique identifier for the specific template.

definition.description: A single document storing the detailed layout and content definition for the parent Template. This is a 1:1 relationship with the Template. It includes denormalized 'createdByUserId' (from the parent Template) for authorization independence, ensuring access is tied to the parent Template's owner.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns the parent template and this content.

params.name: templateId
params.description: The unique identifier of the parent template to which this content belongs.

firestore.reasoning:
The proposed Firestore structure prioritizes robust security, scalability, and debuggability by strictly adhering to the core design principles and mandates. User-created templates and their associated content are stored in a hierarchical structure under the user's specific path, ensuring clear ownership and simplified authorization.

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):**
1.  **Template Document (`/users/{userId}/templates/{templateId}`):** The `Template` document inherently contains `createdByUserId`. For access control, security rules will directly compare `request.auth.uid` against the `userId` in the path and the `resource.data.createdByUserId` field. This eliminates any need for `get()` calls to infer ownership.
2.  **Document Template Content (`/users/{userId}/templates/{templateId}/documentTemplateContent/document`):** The `DocumentTemplateContent` entity, being a 1:1 child of `Template`, will denormalize the `createdByUserId` field from its parent `Template`. This critical denormalization allows security rules to evaluate access to the content document solely based on its own fields and the path parameters (`userId`), without needing to perform a `get()` operation on the parent `Template` document. This design choice directly fulfills the Authorization Independence mandate, making atomic operations simpler and rules easier to write and debug.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
1.  **Structural Segregation:** By placing user-specific templates and their content under `/users/{userId}/...`, the structure naturally segregates data by owner. This means that a `list` operation on `/users/{userId}/templates` will only return templates belonging to `request.auth.uid` when rules are correctly written (e.g., `allow list: if request.auth.uid == userId;`). The security rules enforce access based on the path, rather than filtering a larger, insecure collection post-query. This ensures that the client-side queries will only ever receive data they are authorized to see, preventing accidental data leakage and adhering to the QAP principle.
